purpose: Canonical specification for how every other blueprint in this repository should be named, structured, maintained, validated and used.
filename_rule: Every standalone blueprint file ends in -blueprint.json. The descriptive subject comes first: finance-debt-blueprint.json, technology-system-blueprint.json, culture-subculture-blueprint.json.

record_schema_contract.identity: Stable identifiers, names, aliases and classification boundaries.
record_schema_contract.time: Valid time, observation time, publication/retrieval time and versioning where relevant.
record_schema_contract.geography: Location, jurisdiction, scale and cross-border scope where relevant.
record_schema_contract.function: What the entity/system does or represents.
record_schema_contract.organization: Actors, institutions, ownership, governance or operational roles where relevant.
record_schema_contract.population_or_users: People, users, affected populations, membership or audience where relevant.
record_schema_contract.dependencies: Inputs, suppliers, infrastructure, technology, finance, regulation or ecological dependencies.
record_schema_contract.relationships: Typed, directional relationships that can be represented as graph edges.
record_schema_contract.evidence: Source, source type, methodology, date and confidence.
record_schema_contract.change: Lifecycle, turning points, succession, failure, reform or transition.

validation_rules: A blueprint does not contain invented observations merely to satisfy its schema.
Sensitive private information is excluded unless there is a documented public-interest reason and lawful public source.
Empirical claims and project-defined symbolic interpretation remain distinguishable.
acquisition_plan: Normalize dates, units, geography and classifications.
Record provenance at observation level where practical.
Instantiate records without filling unknowns with guesses.
implementation_notes: This repository is static-first: blueprints are specifications, not runtime databases.
Do not make frontend pages fetch every blueprint individually; use generated indexes/manifests for navigation.
If a blueprint is split, keep one canonical owner and make derived layers explicitly point back to it.
Do not add a new blueprint merely because a few records need two extra fields; add one when the domain has distinct entity boundaries, acquisition logic, relationships or validation rules.

When renaming a blueprint, update every producer, registry, generated record and validator in the same change. Broken historical paths are preferable to silent ambiguity only after compatibility requirements have been assessed.
The stability audit should treat missing blueprint references as failures, not warnings, once the migration is complete.
quality_bar: A good blueprint makes the next research task obvious: what to collect, from where, how to normalize it, what relationships to create, how to validate it, and what uncertainty must remain visible.
